title: Bluetooth LE and Classic: GATT, SPP, connections, and compatibility

spans.text: Bluetooth connects phones, sensors, controls, and computers over short-range radio. LE and Classic share a brand but use different profiles and design goals.

BLE is designed for low energy. A peripheral advertises GATT services/characteristics; a central scans, connects, reads/writes, and receives notifications. It suits sensors, setup, battery devices, and BLE Mesh. Bluetooth Classic BR/EDR supports continuous streams and profiles such as SPP serial, A2DP audio, and HID input. ESP-IDF Bluedroid supports both stacks; NimBLE is BLE-only. Arduino `BluetoothSerial` SPP is available only on ESP32 chips with Classic Bluetooth, notably the original ESP32; ESP32-S3/C3/C6/H2 do not all support Classic BT/SPP.

The sketch provides a paired text terminal using SerialBT. BLE uses GATT characteristics and notifications instead; GATT is not the SPP protocol. Check RAM, concurrent radio use, range, and phone compatibility.

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: This sketch requires a chip and core configuration with Classic BT/SPP. Use authenticated, encrypted pairing for sensitive control; never trust a command solely because it arrived over Bluetooth.
